title: Temurah 33
description: Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish test their readings of “standing and valuation” against Rav’s derivations, two baraitot on consecrated animals that died, and a mishna in Bekhorot; then the mishna begins its list of forbidden items that are buried and those that are burned.
topics: 📜 “Of which they may not bring an offering”: the blemished animal, and only a permanent blemish
⚖️ “Whether good or bad”: Rav’s derivations for Reish Lakish and for Rabbi Shimon, and the word “it”
🐓 Levi’s baraita: everything was included, even undomesticated animals and birds
🔄 Two baraitot on animals that died: blemished from the outset, or consecrated before the blemish?
🐕 Redeeming sacrificial animals to feed them to dogs? Only where one transgressed and slaughtered them
🐄 Rav on the mishna in Bekhorot: “This is the statement of Rabbi Shimon”, or “and his disputants”?
⛏️ The mishna: items that are buried
🔥 The mishna: items that are burned

a1.he: הָא מָה אֲנִי מְקַיֵּים ״וְאִם כׇּל בְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר לֹא יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה קׇרְבָּן לַה׳״ — בְּבַעֲלֵי מוּמִין שֶׁיִּפָּדוּ.

a2.he: יָכוֹל יִפָּדוּ עַל מוּם עוֹבֵר? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אֲשֶׁר לֹא יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה״ — שֶׁאֵינָהּ קְרֵיבָה כׇּל עִיקָּר, יָצְתָה זוֹ שֶׁאֵינָהּ קְרֵיבָה הַיּוֹם אֶלָּא לְמָחָר.

a3.he: וְאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא: עֲבֵיד לַהּ הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה.

a4.he: אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל, אָמַר רַב: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, דְּאָמַר לְרַבָּנַן קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה, קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ לֹא הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה? דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״וְהֶעֱרִיךְ הַכֹּהֵן אוֹתָהּ בֵּין טוֹב וּבֵין רָע״.

a5.he: אֵיזֶהוּ דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ חָלוּק בֵּין טוֹב לְרַע? הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר: זֶה קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת, וְאָמַר קְרָא ״אוֹתָהּ״ לְמַעוֹטֵי קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ.

a6.he: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, ״אוֹתָהּ״ לְמַעוֹטֵי מַאי? לְמַעוֹטֵי בַּעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ.

a7.he: וּלְתַנָּא דְּבֵי לֵוִי, דְּאָמַר דַּאֲפִילּוּ בַּעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה, דְּתָנֵי לֵוִי: הַכֹּל הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה, וַאֲפִילּוּ בַּעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ, וְכֵן תָּנֵי לֵוִי בְּמַתְנִיתֵיהּ: וַאֲפִילּוּ חַיָּה, וַאֲפִילּוּ עוֹפוֹת, וְהָכְתִיב ״אוֹתָהּ״! קַשְׁיָא.

a8.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַב: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּאָמַר, קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה, קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת לֹא הָיוּ? דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״וְהֶעֱרִיךְ הַכֹּהֵן אוֹתָהּ בֵּין טוֹב וּבֵין רָע״, אֵיזֶהוּ דָּבָר שֶׁחָלוּק בֵּין טוֹב וּבֵין רָע? הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר: זֶה קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ, וְאָמַר קְרָא ״אוֹתָהּ״ לְמַעוֹטֵי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת.

a9.he: אִי הָכִי, ״בֵּין טוֹב לְרָע״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ! קַשְׁיָא.

a10.he: מֵיתִיבִי: מֵתוּ תְּמִימִין — יִקָּבְרוּ, וּבַעֲלֵי מוּמִין — יִפָּדוּ. בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים? בְּקׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ, אֲבָל בְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת — בֵּין תְּמִימִין בֵּין בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִים יִקָּבֵרוּ.

a11.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֶחָד קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ וְאֶחָד קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת, תְּמִימִים — יִקָּבְרוּ, בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין — יִפָּדוּ. תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מֵרֵישָׁא!

a12.he: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הָכָא בְמַאי עָסְקִינַן? בְּבַעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ.

a13.he: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּאִי תֵּימָא שֶׁקָּדַם הֶקְדֵּישָׁן אֶת מוּמָן — לִיפְלוֹג רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן עֲלַהּ, אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינָּה בְּבַעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ.

a14.he: אֶלָּא, לֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתֵּיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ!

a15.he: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מוֹקֵים לַהּ בְּשֶׁקָּדַם הֶקְדֵּישָׁן אֶת מוּמָן, אִי הָכִי, נִיפְלוֹג רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן עֲלַהּ.

a16.he: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מֵיפָךְ אָפֵיךְ, וְהָכִי מוֹתֵיב מִמְּכִילְתָּא אַחֲרִיתִי: מֵתוּ, בֵּין תְּמִימִין בֵּין בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין — יִקָּבֵרוּ. [בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים? בְּקׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ, אֲבָל בְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת — יִפָּדוּ.]

a17.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: תְּמִימִים — יִקָּבְרוּ, וּבַעֲלֵי מוּמִין — יִפָּדוּ. תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִסֵּיפָא!

a18.he: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הָכָא בְמַאי עָסְקִינַן? בְּבַעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ. הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּאִי תֵּימָא בְּשֶׁקָּדַם הֶקְדֵּישָׁן אֶת מוּמָן — נִיפְלוֹג רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן עֲלַהּ.

a19.he: אֶלָּא לֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתֵּיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ! אָמַר לָךְ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: הָכָא בְמַאי עָסְקִינַן — בְּשֶׁקָּדַם הֶקְדֵּישָׁן אֶת מוּמָן. וְנִיפְלוֹג רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן עֲלַהּ! אָמַר לָךְ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: הָכִי נָמֵי דִּפְלִיג רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.

a20.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא: לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, דְּאָמַר לְרַבָּנַן: קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ לֹא הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה, וְקָתָנֵי ״קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ

b1.he: בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין יִפָּדוּ״, וּמוֹקְמִינַן לָהּ בְּשֶׁקָּדַם הֶקְדֵּישָׁן אֶת מוּמָן, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ פּוֹדִין אֶת הַקֳּדָשִׁים לְהַאֲכִילָן לִכְלָבִים!

b3.he: כִּדְתַנְיָא: כׇּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁנָּפַל בָּהֶן מוּם, וּשְׁחָטָן, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: יִקָּבֵרוּ, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: יִפָּדוּ.

b4.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא: לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, דְּאָמַר: קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת לֹא הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה, אַמַּאי תְּמִימִים יִקָּבֵרוּ? מִשּׁוּם דַּחֲזוּ לְהַקְרָבָה.

b5.he: כִּדְתַנְיָא: הַמַּתְפִּיס תְּמִימִים לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת, כְּשֶׁהֵן נִפְדִּין — אֵינָן נִפְדִּין אֶלָּא לַמִּזְבֵּחַ, שֶׁכׇּל הָרָאוּי לַמִּזְבֵּחַ אֵינוֹ יוֹצֵא מִידֵי מִזְבֵּחַ לְעוֹלָם.

b6.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רָבָא: לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, דְּמוֹקֵים לַהּ בְּבַעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ, וְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא סְבִירָא לְהוּ דְּבַעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ דְּלָא הָוֵי בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה. וְלָא?!

b7.he: וְהָתְנַן: כׇּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁקָּדַם מוּם קָבוּעַ לְהֶקְדֵּשָׁן וְנִפְדּוּ, חַיָּיבִין בַּבְּכוֹרָה וּבַמַּתָּנוֹת, וְיוֹצְאִין לְחוּלִּין לִיגָּזֵז וְלֵיעָבֵד.

b8.he: וְלָדָן וַחֲלָבָן מוּתָּר לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנָן, וְהַשּׁוֹחֲטָן בַּחוּץ פָּטוּר, וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה, וְאִם מֵתוּ יִפָּדוּ.

b9.he: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַב: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, דְּאָמַר קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה, קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת לֹא הָיוּ, כְּדִתְנַן: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת אִם מֵתוּ יִפָּדוּ.

b10.he: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּבַעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ שֶׁנִּפְדֶּה, מַאי טַעְמָא? דַּאֲמַר קְרָא: ״אוֹתָהּ״, ״אוֹתָהּ״ לְמַעוֹטֵי בַּעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ. אֲבָל חֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֲפִילּוּ בַּעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ הָיָה בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה!

b11.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאן חֲכָמִים? תַּנָּא דְּבֵי לֵוִי. אִי הָכִי, ״זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן״ וְתוּ לָא? ״זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וּמַחְלוּקְתּוֹ״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!

b12.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַאי דְּלָא קָתָנֵי הָכִי, מִשּׁוּם דְּרַב סָבַר לַהּ כְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, דְּאָמַר לְרַבָּנַן: קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה, קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ לֹא הָיוּ.

b13.he: וְרֵישָׁא קָתָנֵי: ״וְאִם מֵתוּ יִפָּדוּ״, וְסֵיפָא קָתָנֵי: ״אִם מֵתוּ יִקָּבֵרוּ״.

b14.he: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, רַב כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ, וּדְקָא קַשְׁיָא לָךְ ״זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וּמַחְלוּקְתּוֹ״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ, אֵימָא הָכִי נָמֵי.

b15.he: מַתְנִי׳ וְאֵלּוּ הֵן הַנִּקְבָּרִין: קָדָשִׁים שֶׁהִפִּילוּ — יִקָּבֵרוּ, הִפִּילָה שִׁלְיָא — תִּקָּבֵר, וְשׁוֹר הַנִּסְקָל, וְעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה, וְצִפֳּרֵי מְצוֹרָע, וְשֵׂיעַר נָזִיר,

b16.he: וּפֶטֶר חֲמוֹר, וּבָשָׂר בְּחָלָב, וְחוּלִּין שֶׁנִּשְׁחֲטוּ בַּעֲזָרָה. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: חוּלִּין שֶׁנִּשְׁחֲטוּ בַּעֲזָרָה יִשָּׂרֵפוּ, וְכֵן חַיָּה שֶׁנִּשְׁחֲטָה בַּעֲזָרָה.

b17.he: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן הַנִּשְׂרָפִין: חָמֵץ בַּפֶּסַח — יִשָּׂרֵף, וּתְרוּמָה טְמֵאָה, וְהָעׇרְלָה, וְכִלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם, אֶת שֶׁדַּרְכָּן לִשָּׂרֵוף — ישרף, וְאֶת שֶׁדַּרְכָּן לְהִקָּבֵר — יִקָּבֵר, וּמַדְלִיקִין בְּפַת וּבְשֶׁמֶן שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה. כׇּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁנִּשְׁחֲטוּ חוּץ לִזְמַנָּן וְחוּץ לִמְקוֹמָן — הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ יִשָּׂרֵפוּ.

messages.text: Continued from 32b: a baraita cited in support of Rabbi Yoḥanan said that the verse “And if it be any non-kosher animal” (Leviticus 27:11) speaks of blemished animals, since a non-kosher animal is stated separately later in the passage (Leviticus 27:27).

But if the halakha of standing and valuation is already mentioned with regard to a non-kosher animal, how do I realize the meaning of the verse: “And if it be any non-kosher animal, of which they may not bring an offering unto the Lord, then he shall set the animal before the priest. And the priest shall value it.” The verse is referring to blemished animals, which are unfit for sacrifice just like non-kosher animals, and it teaches that they can be redeemed.

verse.he: וְאִם כׇּל־בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה אֲשֶׁר לֹא־יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה קׇרְבָּן לַיהֹוָה וְהֶעֱמִיד אֶת־הַבְּהֵמָה לִפְנֵי הַכֹּהֵן׃
verse.en: If [the vow concerns] any impure animal that may not be brought as an offering to GOD, the animal shall be presented before the priest,

notes.dh: הא מה אני מקיים (כל הבהמה) אשר לא יקריב ממנה בבעלי מומין שיפדו
notes.he: ואין לומר דאימא איפכא דקרא דאשר [לא] יקריבו משמע דאינה פסולה אלא להקרבה אבל להדיוט שריא:
notes.en: How do I realize “of which they may not bring an offering”? With blemished animals, that they can be redeemed: And one cannot say, interpret it the other way round, for the verse “of which they may not bring” implies that it is disqualified only from being offered, but is permitted for ordinary use.

messages.text: One might have thought that any blemished animal can be redeemed, even for a temporary blemish. Therefore, the verse states: “Non-kosher animal, of which they may not bring an offering,” which indicates that only a blemished animal that may not be sacrificed at all, i.e., one with a permanent blemish, is redeemed. This animal with a temporary blemish is thereby excluded, as it may not be sacrificed today, but it may be sacrificed tomorrow.

And the Merciful One states that one should perform standing and valuation for a blemished animal, in accordance with the verse “Then he shall set the animal before the priest. And the priest shall value it.” Since the verse requires that the animal have a permanent blemish to be redeemed, it must be referring to an animal consecrated for the altar, as all animals consecrated for Temple maintenance may be redeemed, even unblemished ones.

notes.dh: ואמר רחמנא עביד לה העמדה והערכה
notes.he: דכתיב בתריה והעמיד והעריך וגו' והא ודאי קדשי מזבח היא מדבעינן מום קבוע דאי בדק הבית תמימים נמי מפרקי דמאי איכפת להו אי תם אי בעל מום. אלמא קדשי מזבח נמי היו בכלל העמדה והערכה לרבנן דהא ברייתא רבנן היא דהא סתם סיפרא היא וסתם סיפרא ר' יהודה (בכורות דף סא.) בר פלוגתא דר"ש והיינו כרבי יוחנן. ומהכא שמעינן קדשי מזבח לרבנן וממתני' שמעינן קדשי ב"ה מדקאמר ר"ש קדשי בדק הבית יפדו מכלל דשמעינהו לרבנן דאמרי יקברו:
notes.en: And the Merciful One states: perform standing and valuation for it: as it is written after it, “then he shall set … and shall value.” And this is certainly [an animal] consecrated for the altar, since we require a permanent blemish; for if it were [consecrated for] Temple maintenance, unblemished animals too are redeemed, for what does it matter to them whether it is unblemished or blemished? Evidently, according to the Rabbis, animals consecrated for the altar too were included in standing and valuation, since this baraita is the Rabbis’: it is an unattributed Sifra, and an unattributed Sifra is Rabbi Yehuda (Bekhorot 61a), the disputant of Rabbi Shimon; and this is in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan. And from here we learn [the Rabbis’ view on] animals consecrated for the altar, and from the mishna we learn [their view on] those consecrated for Temple maintenance: since Rabbi Shimon says that those consecrated for Temple maintenance are redeemed, it follows that we have heard the Rabbis say they are buried.

messages.text: Furthermore, as this is an unattributed baraita that appears in the Sifra, it is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, the disputant of Rabbi Shimon, and therefore it follows the opinion of the Rabbis of the mishna. It may therefore be concluded from the baraita that the Rabbis hold that one redeems an animal consecrated for the altar with standing and valuation, as maintained by Rabbi Yoḥanan.

notes.dh: ואמר רחמנא עביד לה העמדה והערכה
notes.he: דבהאי קרא דאשר לא יקריבו כתיב והעמיד והעריך וסתם סיפרא ר' יהודה אלמא רבנן דעלמא אית להו העמדה בקדשי מזבח ובקדשי ב"ה ק"ל ממתניתין מדקאמר ר"ש יפדו מכלל דלרבנן לא יפדו א"נ קדשי ב"ה ק"ל מדכתיב והעמידו הכהן בין טוב ובין רע איזהו דבר שאין חילוק בין טוב לרע הוי אומר זה קדשי ב"ה ר"ש:
notes.en: And the Merciful One states: perform standing and valuation for it: since in this verse, “of which they may not bring,” it is written “then he shall set … and shall value,” and an unattributed Sifra is Rabbi Yehuda. Evidently the Rabbis in general hold that standing applies to animals consecrated for the altar. And [that it applies to] animals consecrated for Temple maintenance we know from the mishna, since Rabbi Shimon says they are redeemed, which implies that according to the Rabbis they are not redeemed. Alternatively, we know [it for] animals consecrated for Temple maintenance from what is written, “And the priest shall value it, whether it be good or bad”: which is an item in which there is no distinction between good and bad? You must say, this is [an item] consecrated for Temple maintenance. [The note ends with the letters ר״ש.]

messages.text: What is the reasoning of Reish Lakish, who said that according to the Rabbis, animals consecrated for Temple maintenance were included in the halakha of standing and valuation, whereas animals consecrated for the altar were not included in the halakha of standing and valuation? The reasoning is that the verse states: “Then he shall set the animal before the priest. And the priest shall value it, whether it be good or bad” (Leviticus 27:12).
messages.lead: § The Gemara analyzes the opinion of Reish Lakish.

verse.he: וְהֶעֱרִיךְ הַכֹּהֵן אֹתָהּ בֵּין טוֹב וּבֵין רָע כְּעֶרְכְּךָ הַכֹּהֵן כֵּן יִהְיֶה׃
verse.en: and the priest shall assess it. Whether high or low, whatever assessment is set by the priest shall stand;

notes.he: משמע אחד טוב ואחד רע דשניהן שוין תם ובעל מום:
notes.en: Whether it be good or bad: implies good and bad alike, that the two are equal, the unblemished and the blemished.

messages.text: What is an item for which the halakha is not divided between good and bad, i.e., where there is no difference between unblemished and blemished animals? You must say that this is an item consecrated for Temple maintenance, which has the same sanctity whether blemished or unblemished. And the verse states: “And the priest shall value it.” The restrictive term “it” serves to exclude animals consecrated for the altar from the halakha of standing and valuation.

notes.he: ולא קאי האי והעמיד והעריך ארישא דקרא דמשתעי בקדשי מזבח:
notes.en: “It” serves to exclude animals consecrated for the altar: and this “then he shall set … and shall value” does not refer back to the first part of the verse, which speaks of animals consecrated for the altar.

notes.he: מ"ט דר' יוחנן דאמר לרבנן אחד זה ואחד זה היו בכלל העמדה והערכה דכתיב ואם כל בהמה טמאה כו' איזהו דבר שאינו חולק בין טוב לרע. כלומר דבין תם ובין בעל מום קדושתו שוה היינו קדשי בדק הבית דאינן אלא לדמים וכתי' אותה והעריך אותה למעוטי קדשי מזבח. ור' יוחנן סבר אותה לרבנן למעוטי בעל מום מעיקרא דאינן בכלל העמדה והערכה. ל"א תנא מאי טעמא דרבי שמעון דאמר קדשי מזבח היו קדשי בדק הבית לא היו כדאמרן לעיל וזה וזה מודים כו':
notes.en: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said that according to the Rabbis both this and that were included in standing and valuation [the daf names Reish Lakish here, and the reasoning that follows is his]? As it is written: “And if it be any non-kosher animal” etc. Which is an item that is not divided between good and bad, that is, whose sanctity is the same whether it is unblemished or blemished? That is [an item] consecrated for Temple maintenance, which is only for its value. And it is written “it”: “and the priest shall value it,” to exclude animals consecrated for the altar. And Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that “it,” according to the Rabbis, serves to exclude an animal blemished from the outset, which is not included in standing and valuation. Another version: [the Gemara] teaches, What is the reasoning of Rabbi Shimon, who said that animals consecrated for the altar were [included] and animals consecrated for Temple maintenance were not, as we said above; and both this one and that one agree, etc.

messages.text: And according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, who says that according to the Rabbis, animals consecrated for the altar are also included in the obligation of standing and valuation, the term “it” serves to exclude what?
It serves to exclude from the halakha of standing and valuation an animal that was blemished from the outset and was consecrated for the altar.

notes.he: אית ליה ודאי דהאי בין טוב ובין רע בקדשי ב"ה קאי ומיהו והעמיד והעריך ארישא דקרא דאוקימנא בקדשי מזבח ואסיפא דמשתעי בב"ה קאי ואותה למעוטי בעל מום מעיקרו בקדשי מזבח. ולר"ל לא צריך בעל מום מעיקרו למעוטי דהוא אמר לרבנן קדשי מזבח לא היו ואפילו קדם הקדישן למומן וכ"ש האי:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yoḥanan: certainly holds that this “whether it be good or bad” refers to animals consecrated for Temple maintenance. But “then he shall set … and shall value” refers both to the first part of the verse, which we established as speaking of animals consecrated for the altar, and to the latter part, which speaks of Temple maintenance; and “it” serves to exclude an animal blemished from the outset among animals consecrated for the altar. And according to Reish Lakish there is no need to exclude an animal blemished from the outset, since he says that according to the Rabbis animals consecrated for the altar were not [included], even where their consecration preceded their blemish, and all the more so this one.

messages.text: But this is problematic according to the tanna of the school of Levi, who said that even an animal that was blemished from the outset is included in the halakha of standing and valuation.
Everything was included in the halakha of standing and valuation, even an animal blemished from the outset.
Even an undomesticated animal, and even birds that are not brought as offerings, e.g., geese, are included in the halakha of standing and valuation.

notes.he: כגון אווזין ותרנגולין דלא שייכי כלל למזבח:
notes.en: And even undomesticated animals and birds: such as geese and chickens, which have no connection to the altar at all.

notes.he: כגון שמתפיס תרנגולין לב"ה והא דאמרינן מנחות (דף ק:) אין לעופות פדיון ה"מ בשקדשה קדושת הגוף למזבח:
notes.en: Even an undomesticated animal and even a bird: for example, where one associates chickens [with a consecration] for Temple maintenance. And that which we say in Menaḥot (100b), “Birds have no redemption,” applies where they were consecrated with inherent sanctity for the altar.

messages.text: But isn’t it written “it,” which must serve to exclude some animal from the obligation of standing and valuation? If so, how can Levi teach that everything is included? Indeed, this poses a difficulty.

What is the reasoning of Rabbi Shimon, who said that animals consecrated for the altar were included in the halakha of standing and valuation, and therefore if they died without redemption they are buried, but animals consecrated for Temple maintenance were not included in this halakha? As the verse states: “Then he shall set the animal before the priest. And the priest shall value it, whether it be good or bad” (Leviticus 27:11–12).
messages.lead: The Gemara discusses the opinion of Rabbi Shimon in the mishna.

verse.he: וְאִם כׇּל־בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה אֲשֶׁר לֹא־יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה קׇרְבָּן לַיהֹוָה וְהֶעֱמִיד אֶת־הַבְּהֵמָה לִפְנֵי הַכֹּהֵן׃ וְהֶעֱרִיךְ הַכֹּהֵן אֹתָהּ בֵּין טוֹב וּבֵין רָע כְּעֶרְכְּךָ הַכֹּהֵן כֵּן יִהְיֶה׃
verse.en: If [the vow concerns] any impure animal that may not be brought as an offering to GOD, the animal shall be presented before the priest, and the priest shall assess it. Whether high or low, whatever assessment is set by the priest shall stand;

messages.text: What is an item for which the halakha is divided between good and bad, i.e., between an unblemished and blemished animal? You must say that this is an animal consecrated for the altar, and the verse states: “And the priest shall value it,” which serves to exclude animals consecrated for Temple maintenance from the halakha of standing and valuation.

If so, that the verse is referring to a consecration for which there is a distinction between good and bad, then it should have stated: And the priest shall value it between good and bad, to indicate that this distinction is made. The term “whether it be good or bad” indicates that the two types have the same halakha, as claimed by the Rabbis. This poses a difficulty for the opinion of Rabbi Shimon.
messages.quote: whether it be good or bad

notes.he: משמע דהוי חילוק בין טוב לרע ובין טוב ובין רע משמע אחד טוב ואחד רע ושניהן שוין:
notes.en: It should have said “between good and bad”: that would imply that there is a distinction between good and bad; but “whether good or bad” implies good and bad alike, the two being equal.

notes.dh: איזהו דבר שחלוק בין טוב לרע
notes.he: בין תם לבעל מום אלו קדשי מזבח דתם קרב ולא בעל מום וכתי' אותה והעריך למעוטי קדשי בדק הבית אי הכי לר' שמעון בין טוב ובין רע בין טוב לרע מיבעי ליה למיכתב אי בקדשי מזבח מיירי קשיא לר' שמעון:
notes.en: Which is an item that is divided between good and bad, between unblemished and blemished? These are animals consecrated for the altar, for an unblemished one is offered and a blemished one is not. And it is written “it”: “and the priest shall value it,” to exclude animals consecrated for Temple maintenance. If so, according to Rabbi Shimon, [instead of] “whether good or bad” it should have written “between good and bad.” If it speaks of animals consecrated for the altar, it is difficult for Rabbi Shimon.

messages.text: With regard to consecrated animals that died, if they were unblemished they are not redeemed and shall be buried, and if they were blemished they can be redeemed. In what case is this statement said? It is said with regard to animals consecrated for the altar. But with regard to animals consecrated for Temple maintenance, both unblemished and blemished animals shall be buried. This is the statement of the Rabbis.
messages.lead: § The Gemara raises an objection to the opinions of Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish from a baraita:

notes.he: אפילו הנך דליתנהו בכלל העמדה והערכה היכא דמתו תמימים עבוד רבנן מעלה דיקברו הואיל והוו חזי להקרבה:
notes.en: If they died unblemished, they shall be buried: even those that are not included in standing and valuation, where they died unblemished, the Rabbis made a stringency that they be buried, since they were fit for sacrifice.

notes.he: קס"ד השתא משום דלא היו בכלל העמדה והערכה:
notes.en: With regard to animals consecrated for the altar: it now enters our mind [that blemished ones are redeemed] because they were not included in standing and valuation.

notes.he: דהיו בהעמדה והערכה:
notes.en: But with regard to animals consecrated for Temple maintenance, etc.: since they were [included] in standing and valuation.

notes.he: השתא ס"ד משום דקדשי מזבח לא היו בכלל העמדה והערכה ותמימים יקברו דאין בהן מום ואין רשאין לפדות בלא מום:
notes.en: Unblemished ones shall be buried; blemished ones can be redeemed: it now enters our mind [that this is] because animals consecrated for the altar were not included in standing and valuation; and unblemished ones are buried because they have no blemish, and one is not permitted to redeem without a blemish.

notes.he: מיתיבי קדשי מזבח תמימים יקברו בעלי מומים יפדו קדשי בדק הבית בין תמימים ובין בעלי מומים יקברו והא ברייתא דייקא כריש לקיש אליבא (דרבי שמעון) [דרבנן] דאמר קדשי בדק הבית היו קדשי מזבח לא היו:
notes.en: They raised an objection: animals consecrated for the altar, unblemished ones are buried and blemished ones are redeemed; animals consecrated for Temple maintenance, both unblemished and blemished ones are buried. And this baraita is precise in accordance with Reish Lakish according to the Rabbis [the printed text reads “according to Rabbi Shimon,” corrected to “the Rabbis”], who said that animals consecrated for Temple maintenance were [included] and animals consecrated for the altar were not.

messages.text: Both in a case where the animals that died were consecrated for the altar and in a case where they were consecrated for Temple maintenance, if they were unblemished they can be buried, and if they were blemished they can be redeemed.

notes.he: משום מעלה:
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon says, etc.: unblemished ones shall be buried: as a stringency.

notes.he: לקמיה פריך היכי קאמר ר"ש קדשי מזבח [יפדו] הא בין רבי יוחנן בין ר"ל אמרי דלר"ש קדשי מזבח הוו בכלל העמדה והערכה:
notes.en: And blemished ones can be redeemed: further on the Gemara asks: how can Rabbi Shimon say that animals consecrated for the altar [are redeemed], when both Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish say that according to Rabbi Shimon animals consecrated for the altar were included in standing and valuation?

notes.he: דכי נמי קדשי ב"ה לא היו כדמפרש לקמן טעמא משום דחזו להקרבה:
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon says: unblemished ones shall be buried: for even though animals consecrated for Temple maintenance were not [included], [they are buried], as the reason is explained below: because they are fit for sacrifice.

messages.text: This is apparently a conclusive refutation of the statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan, from the first clause of the baraita, as Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that according to the Rabbis, both animals consecrated for the altar and those consecrated for Temple maintenance are included in the halakha of standing and valuation and are buried if they died.
messages.quote: if they were blemished they can be redeemed

notes.he: דקתני לרבנן בקדשי מזבח יפדו:
notes.en: A conclusive refutation of Rabbi Yoḥanan from the first clause: which teaches that according to the Rabbis, animals consecrated for the altar are redeemed.

notes.dh: ר' שמעון אומר אחד קדשי כו'
notes.he: מאי לאו בתם דקתני בעלי מומין יפדו לא בשקדם הקדישן מומן קתני וקשיא לר' יוחנן מרישא דברייתא דקתני בעלי מומין יפדו דהא ר' יוחנן אמר לרבנן בין קדשי מזבח בין קדשי בדק הבית היו בכלל העמדה והערכה דיקברו ומיירי בשקדם הקדישן את מומן והא ברייתא קתני יפדו [ותיובתא לרבי יוחנן מרישא:
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon says: Both animals consecrated, etc. Is it not speaking of one that was unblemished [when consecrated], when it teaches that blemished ones are redeemed? Is it not teaching [a case] where their consecration preceded their blemish? And it is difficult for Rabbi Yoḥanan from the first clause of the baraita, which teaches that blemished ones are redeemed; for Rabbi Yoḥanan said that according to the Rabbis both animals consecrated for the altar and those consecrated for Temple maintenance were included in standing and valuation, so that they are buried, and [the baraita] speaks of where their consecration preceded their blemish, yet this baraita teaches that they are redeemed. And it is a conclusive refutation of Rabbi Yoḥanan from the first clause.

messages.text: Rabbi Yoḥanan could say to you: What are we dealing with here? We are dealing with an animal that was blemished from the outset. In such a case, the Rabbis rule that the animal was not included in the halakha of standing and valuation and is therefore redeemed if it dies. But a consecrated animal that subsequently developed a blemish and died must be buried.

notes.he: משום הכי יפדו ובקדשי ב"ה יקברו דהתם לא שני בין בעל מום מעיקרו לקדם הקדישו למומו:
notes.en: With an animal blemished from the outset: that is why they are redeemed, while those consecrated for Temple maintenance are buried, for there no distinction is made between an animal blemished from the outset and one whose consecration preceded its blemish.

notes.dh: הכא במאי עסקינן בבעל מום מעיקרו
notes.he: ואפ"ה בקדשי ב"ה יקברו דבכל ענין היו דלא שייך לפלוגי בין תם מעיקרו לבעל מום מעיקרו הואיל ואינן עומדות אלא לדמיהן:
notes.en: What are we dealing with here? With an animal blemished from the outset: and even so, animals consecrated for Temple maintenance are buried, since they were [included] in every case; for it is not relevant to distinguish between one that was unblemished at the outset and one blemished from the outset, since they stand only for their value.

notes.dh: אמר לך ר' יוחנן רישא במאי עסקינן
notes.he: דיפדו בבעל מום מעיקרא דדברי הכל לא היו בכלל העמדה והערכה:
notes.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan could say to you: What are we dealing with here in the first clause, that they are redeemed? With animals blemished from the outset, which according to everyone were not included in standing and valuation.

messages.text: So too, it is reasonable that the baraita is discussing animals blemished from the outset, as, if you say that it is referring to animals whose consecrations preceded their blemishes, then Rabbi Shimon should disagree with the Rabbis on this point and maintain that such blemished animals consecrated for the altar should be buried, not redeemed. After all, Rabbi Shimon holds that animals consecrated for the altar are included in the halakha of standing and valuation. Rather, must one not conclude from this that the baraita is dealing with an animal that is blemished from the outset?
messages.quote: Both consecrated for the altar and consecrated for Temple maintenance

notes.dh: והכי מסתברא דאי בשקדם הקדישו את מומו
notes.he: וטעמייהו דרבנן כדר"ל דקדשי מזבח לא היו בכלל העמדה והערכה ליפלוג ר"ש עלה ולימא בקדשי מזבח יקברו דהא לר"ש קדשי מזבח היו בהעמדה והערכה אלא מדלא פליג ש"מ בבעל מום מעיקרו קאי ומשום הכי קדשי מזבח יפדו וקדשי ב"ה נמי יפדו דלר"ש (נמי) קדשי ב"ה לא היו:
notes.en: So too it is reasonable, for if [it speaks] where their consecration preceded their blemish: and the Rabbis’ reason is as Reish Lakish says, that animals consecrated for the altar were not included in standing and valuation, then Rabbi Shimon should disagree with it and say that animals consecrated for the altar are buried, since according to Rabbi Shimon animals consecrated for the altar were [included] in standing and valuation. Rather, since he does not disagree, conclude from it that it refers to an animal blemished from the outset; and that is why animals consecrated for the altar are redeemed, and animals consecrated for Temple maintenance are also redeemed, since according to Rabbi Shimon animals consecrated for Temple maintenance were not [included].

notes.he: דבבעל מום מעיקרא דאי בשקדם הקדישן את מומן קאמר יפדו]:
notes.en: So too it is reasonable that it is with an animal blemished from the outset; for if it says they are redeemed where their consecration preceded their blemish…

notes.he: ולימא יקברו דהא אמרן זה וזה מודין דלר' שמעון דקדשי מזבח היו בכלל העמדה והערכה:
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon should disagree with the first clause and say that they are buried, since we said that both this one and that one agree that according to Rabbi Shimon animals consecrated for the altar were included in standing and valuation.

messages.text: But if the baraita is referring to animals blemished from the outset, and for this reason the Rabbis hold that the animal is redeemed, then it may be inferred that the Rabbis maintain that if the animal developed a blemish after its consecration and died, it must be buried. If so, let us say that the baraita is a conclusive refutation of the opinion of Reish Lakish, who maintains that according to the Rabbis, animals consecrated for the altar were not included in the halakha of standing and valuation and are redeemed if they died.

notes.he: דהא מגופה שמעינן דאבעל מום מעיקרו קאי והשתא י"ל טעמא דבעל מום מעיקרו הא קדם הקדישו למומו לרבנן נמי יקברו:
notes.en: Let us say it is a conclusive refutation of Reish Lakish: since from the baraita itself we learn that it refers to an animal blemished from the outset; and now one can say: the reason is that it was blemished from the outset, but where its consecration preceded its blemish, according to the Rabbis too they are buried.

notes.he: ל"א קשיא סיפא לר"ש דמתני' דקאמר סיפא דהא ברייתא ר' שמעון אמר אחד קדשי מזבח ואחד קדשי בדק הבית תמימים יקברו בעלי מומין יפדו וקשיא דרבי שמעון אדרבי שמעון דהא ר' שמעון קאמר לעיל קדשי מזבח היו אלא לאו ש"מ סיפא נמי דקאמר ר' שמעון בעלי מומין יפדו בבעל מום מעיקרא קאמר דלא היו בכלל העמדה והערכה. והשתא קא דייק ברייתא אבל בשקדם הקדישן את מומן מאי בעי העמדה והערכה נימא תיהוי תיובתא דריש לקיש דהא אמר לעיל דלרבנן קדשי מזבח לא היו:
notes.en: Another version: the latter clause is difficult for Rabbi Shimon of the mishna, since in the latter clause of this baraita it says: “Rabbi Shimon says: Both animals consecrated for the altar and animals consecrated for Temple maintenance, unblemished ones are buried and blemished ones are redeemed”; and Rabbi Shimon contradicts Rabbi Shimon, since Rabbi Shimon said above that animals consecrated for the altar were [included]. Rather, must one not conclude from it that in the latter clause too, where Rabbi Shimon says blemished ones are redeemed, he is speaking of an animal blemished from the outset, which was not included in standing and valuation? And now he infers from the baraita: but where their consecration preceded their blemish, what [is the law]? It requires standing and valuation. Let us say it is a conclusive refutation of Reish Lakish, since he said above that according to the Rabbis animals consecrated for the altar were not [included].

messages.text: Reish Lakish interprets the baraita as referring to animals whose consecrations preceded their blemishes. Consequently, the statement of the Rabbis is in accordance with his opinion that animals consecrated for the altar were not included in the halakha of standing and valuation and are therefore redeemed if they died.

notes.he: וטעמייהו דרבנן משום דקדשי מזבח לא היו:
notes.en: Where their consecration preceded their blemish: and the Rabbis’ reason is that animals consecrated for the altar were not [included].

notes.dh: ריש לקיש מוקים לה לעיל לרבנן בשקדם הקדישן את מומן
notes.he: ואפי' הכי לרבנן קדשי מזבח לא היו ואף הכא נמי לא היו אלא יפדו:
notes.en: Reish Lakish establishes it above, according to the Rabbis, where their consecration preceded their blemish; and even so, according to the Rabbis, animals consecrated for the altar were not [included], and here too they were not, and so they are redeemed.

messages.text: If so, then the earlier question recurs, as Rabbi Shimon should disagree with the statement of the Rabbis and say that such blemished animals consecrated for the altar are buried.

notes.he: דקדשי מזבח ונימא יקברו ואמאי קתני לר"ש אחד קדשי מזבח וא' קדשי ב"ה יפדו:
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon should disagree with it: regarding animals consecrated for the altar, and say that they are buried. So why does it teach that according to Rabbi Shimon both animals consecrated for the altar and those consecrated for Temple maintenance are redeemed?

notes.he: אי הכי הדר קושיין דליפלוג ר' שמעון ברישא דהא אמר קדשי מזבח היו ועוד קשיא סיפא דר' שמעון ארישא:
notes.en: If so, our difficulty returns: Rabbi Shimon should disagree in the first clause, since he said that animals consecrated for the altar were [included]. And further, the latter clause, Rabbi Shimon’s, is difficult against the first clause.

messages.text: Reish Lakish reverses the text of that baraita, i.e., he maintains that in that baraita, Rabbi Shimon explicitly states that animals consecrated for the altar are buried, whether they are unblemished or blemished.

notes.dh: ומשני ר"ל מיפך אפיך והכי מותיב ממכילתא אחריתי
notes.he: דאשכח ברייתא אחריתי דמהפך לה ומותיב לה הכי לר' יוחנן דרשב"ל לא מייתי לה להא תיובתא לר' יוחנן כדגרסי' לה הכא דקתני בר"ש בהדיא קדשי מזבח יפדו:
notes.en: And Reish Lakish answers: he reverses it, and raises the objection like this from another collection: for he found another baraita that reverses it, and he raises the objection to Rabbi Yoḥanan from it in this way. For Reish Lakish does not bring this objection against Rabbi Yoḥanan as we read [the baraita] here, since it teaches explicitly according to Rabbi Shimon that animals consecrated for the altar are redeemed.

notes.dh: רבי שב"ל מפיק ותני במכילתין אחריתי
notes.he: והך דלעיל משבשתא אלא בין תמימין בין בעלי מומין יקברו ומיירי בקדשי ב"ה וכדרבנן דאמרי שהיו [בכלל כו'] ר"ש אומר [תמימים] יקברו כדאמר לקמן משום דחזו להקרבה ומחמירין ביה קדושת מזבח במה דברים אמורים בקדשי ב"ה אתאן לת"ק ולכך אמר יקברו אבל קדשי מזבח כו' רש"א תמימין יקברו אבל בעלי מומין יפדו דלא היו בכלל העמדה תיובתא דרבי יוחנן אמר לך רבי יוחנן כו' תיובתא דרשב"ל ה"נ דפליג ר"ש ודקדק רש"י דברייתא קמייתא נמי נימא הכי ומאי אולמיה דהאי בתרייתא וי"ל דלא דמי דהא אקמייתא ליכא למימר הכי דאם בעלי מומין דת"ק מיירי שהוממו אחר הקדשן ובקדשי מזבח סברא הוא לומר דר' שמעון דקאמר במילתיה אחד קדשי מזבח יפדו בבעלי מומין דתנא קמא מיירי שהוממו אחר שהוקדשו אבל בהך בתרייתא דר"ש לא איירי במילתיה כלל בקדשי מזבח ובחד מילתיה הוא דרבנן דאמר אבל בקדשי מזבח בעלי מומין יפדו מיירי שפיר בשקדם הקדשן ור"ש פליג עלייהו אבל לכך שנה התנא למילתיה משום דבמילתיה לא הזכיר כלל קדשי מזבח ולא גילה בדעתו כלל מה אומר בקדשי מזבח:
notes.en: Reish Lakish removes it and teaches [it] from another collection: and the one above is erroneous. Rather [the baraita reads]: “Whether unblemished or blemished, they shall be buried,” and it speaks of animals consecrated for Temple maintenance, in accordance with the Rabbis, who say that they were [included, etc.]. “Rabbi Shimon says: [Unblemished ones] shall be buried,” as is said below, because they are fit for sacrifice, and one treats them stringently with the sanctity of the altar. “In what case is this statement said? With regard to animals consecrated for Temple maintenance”: this returns to the first tanna, and that is why he said “buried”; “but animals consecrated for the altar, etc.” “Rabbi Shimon says: Unblemished ones shall be buried, but blemished ones can be redeemed,” since they were not included in standing. “A conclusive refutation of Rabbi Yoḥanan”; “Rabbi Yoḥanan could say to you, etc.”; “A conclusive refutation of Reish Lakish”; “Indeed, Rabbi Shimon disagrees.” And Rashi pointed out that for the first baraita too we could say so; so what advantage does this latter one have? One can say that they are not alike, for of the first one this cannot be said. If the first tanna’s blemished animals were ones that became blemished after their consecration, and [the ruling] concerns animals consecrated for the altar, it is reasonable to say that Rabbi Shimon, who says in his own statement “both animals consecrated for the altar [and those for Temple maintenance] are redeemed,” is speaking of the first tanna’s blemished animals, which became blemished after they were consecrated. But in this latter baraita, Rabbi Shimon does not speak of animals consecrated for the altar at all in his statement; it is in the separate statement of the Rabbis, who say “but with regard to animals consecrated for the altar, blemished ones are redeemed,” that it fits well [to speak of] where their consecration preceded [their blemish], and Rabbi Shimon disagrees with them. And the tanna taught his statement this way because in it he did not mention animals consecrated for the altar at all, and did not reveal at all what he says about them.

notes.he: תני בסיפא דהא ברייתא בקדשי מזבח ר' שמעון אמר בין תמימין ובין בעלי מומין יקברו ולא קשיין:
notes.en: Reish Lakish could say to you: teach in the latter clause of this baraita, regarding animals consecrated for the altar, that Rabbi Shimon says: whether unblemished or blemished, they are buried; and there is no difficulty.

messages.text: With regard to consecrated animals that died, whether they were unblemished or blemished, they shall be buried.
messages.lead: And he raises his objection to the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan from another baraita, like this:

notes.dh: אלא מיפך אפיך והכי מותיב לה כדאשכחנא במכילתא אחריתי בין תמימים כו'
notes.he: ואע"ג דבין האי לישנא ללישנא דלעיל כי דייקת בה ליכא מידי אלא (לאו) דקתני בהדיא לר"ש קדשי מזבח יפדו:
notes.en: Rather, he reverses it, and raises the objection to it as we found in another collection: “whether unblemished,” etc.: And although, when you examine it closely, there is no difference between this version and the version above, except that [the first one] teaches explicitly that according to Rabbi Shimon animals consecrated for the altar are redeemed.

notes.he: ל"א ריש לקיש מיפך אפיך הא ברייתא והכי מותיב ממכילתא ברייתא אחריתי והכי מותיב מיתיבי מתו בין תמימין בין בעלי מומין יקברו. רבי שמעון אמר תמימין יקברו בעלי מומין יפדו:
notes.en: Another version: Reish Lakish reverses this baraita, and raises the objection like this from a collection, another baraita. And he raises the objection like this: They raised an objection: “If they died, whether unblemished or blemished, they shall be buried. Rabbi Shimon says: Unblemished ones are buried, blemished ones are redeemed.”

messages.text: With regard to what case is this ruling stated? It is stated with regard to animals consecrated for the altar, but in the case of animals consecrated for Temple maintenance, they can be redeemed. This is the statement of the Rabbis.

notes.he: בד"א. דבין תמימין בין בעלי מומין יקברו בקדשי בדק הבית אבל בקדשי מזבח [בע"מ יפדו] והא דייקא כר"ל אליבא דרבנן:
notes.en: In what case is this statement said: he returns to the first tanna. In what case is this statement said, that whether unblemished or blemished they are buried? With regard to animals consecrated for Temple maintenance; but with regard to animals consecrated for the altar, [blemished ones are redeemed]. And this is precise in accordance with Reish Lakish according to the Rabbis.

messages.text: Rashi, Tosafot and Rabbeinu Gershom read this clause the other way round: the burial of unblemished and blemished animals alike is said of animals consecrated for Temple maintenance, while blemished animals consecrated for the altar can be redeemed. The Gemara’s analysis that follows (Rabbi Yoḥanan refuted “from the latter clause”) treats the Rabbis as ruling that animals consecrated for the altar are redeemed.
With regard to animals consecrated for Temple maintenance that died, if they were unblemished they shall be buried, and if they were blemished they can be redeemed.

notes.he: דקאמר ת"ק בעלי מומין יקברו בקדשי ב"ה אבל קדשי מזבח יפדו דלא היו בהעמדה והערכה ואתא ר' שמעון לחלוק בקדשי ב"ה דאמרת יקברו לדידי יפדו:
notes.en: In what case is this statement said: that the first tanna says blemished ones are buried? With regard to animals consecrated for Temple maintenance; but animals consecrated for the altar are redeemed, since they were not [included] in standing and valuation. And Rabbi Shimon comes to disagree about animals consecrated for Temple maintenance: you said they are buried; according to me they are redeemed.

messages.text: This is apparently a conclusive refutation of the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan, from the latter clause of the statement of the Rabbis in this baraita. According to the baraita, the Rabbis rule that animals consecrated for the altar are redeemed, whereas according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, the Rabbis maintain that animals consecrated for the altar are buried.

notes.he: דקתני לת"ק אבל בקדשי מזבח יפדו:
notes.en: A conclusive refutation of Rabbi Yoḥanan from this latter clause: which teaches, according to the first tanna: but animals consecrated for the altar are redeemed.

notes.dh: מאי לאו בשקדם הקדישן את מומן
notes.he: מיירי ותיובתא דר' יוחנן מהא סיפא דבד"א:
notes.en: Is it not where their consecration preceded their blemish that it speaks? And it is a conclusive refutation of Rabbi Yoḥanan from this latter clause, “In what case.”

messages.text: Rabbi Yoḥanan could say to you: What are we dealing with here? We are dealing with an animal that was blemished from the outset.

notes.he: ובב"ה יקבר דהתם לא שני לן בין תם מעיקרו לבעל מום מעיקרו:
notes.en: With an animal blemished from the outset: and [an animal consecrated for] Temple maintenance is buried, since there we make no distinction between one that was unblemished at the outset and one blemished from the outset.

notes.dh: אמר לך ר' יוחנן הכא במאי עסקינן דבבעל מום יפדו
notes.he: בבעלי מומין מעיקרא:
notes.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan could say to you: What are we dealing with here, that blemished ones are redeemed? With animals blemished from the outset.

messages.text: So, too, it is reasonable that the baraita is referring to animals blemished from the outset, as, if you say that it is dealing with animals whose consecrations preceded their blemishes, and the Rabbis hold that animals consecrated for Temple maintenance are buried whereas those consecrated for the altar are redeemed, then Rabbi Shimon should disagree with the statement of the Rabbis on both accounts, rather than disagreeing merely in the case of animals consecrated for Temple maintenance.

notes.he: ונימא תרתי קדשי ב"ה יפדו וקדשי מזבח יקברו אלא מדלא פליג אלא בקדשי ב"ה דקאמרי אינהו יקברו ואינהו יפדו ובקדשי מזבח שתיק ממאי דאמרי רבנן יפדו ש"מ בבעל מום מעיקרו איירי:
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon should disagree with it: and say two things: animals consecrated for Temple maintenance are redeemed, and animals consecrated for the altar are buried. Rather, since he disagrees only about animals consecrated for Temple maintenance, where they say buried and he says redeemed, while about animals consecrated for the altar he is silent regarding what the Rabbis say, that they are redeemed, conclude from it that it speaks of an animal blemished from the outset.

notes.he: דאי לא תימא הכי ניפלוג ר' שמעון בקדשי מזבח דבעלי מומין יקברו דהא אית ליה קדשי מזבח היו:
notes.en: So too it is reasonable: for if you do not say so, Rabbi Shimon should disagree regarding animals consecrated for the altar, that blemished ones are buried, since he holds that animals consecrated for the altar were [included].

notes.he: בבעלי מומין מעיקרא מיירי:
notes.en: Rather, conclude from it: it speaks of animals blemished from the outset.

messages.text: But if so, let us say that the baraita is a conclusive refutation of the opinion of Reish Lakish, as Rabbi Shimon does not disagree with the Rabbis in the case of animals consecrated for the altar.
Reish Lakish could say to you: What are we dealing with here? We are dealing with animals whose consecrations preceded their blemishes.
But in that case, Rabbi Shimon should disagree with the Rabbis.

Reish Lakish could say to you: Indeed, Rabbi Shimon disagrees with the Rabbis even with regard to animals consecrated for the altar. The baraita mentions Rabbi Shimon’s opinion only with regard to consecrations for Temple maintenance, but he also disagrees with regard to consecrations for the altar.

notes.he: ותנא לך פלוגתייהו בב"ה וה"ה דפליג עלייהו נמי בקדשי מזבח דיקברו:
notes.en: Indeed, he disagrees: and the tanna taught you their dispute about Temple maintenance, and the same is true that he disagrees with them also about animals consecrated for the altar, [saying] that they are buried.

notes.dh: אבל אי בשקדם הקדישן את מומן מאי בעי העמדה והערכה נימא תיהוי כו'
notes.he: כדאמרן לעיל. אי הכי ניפלוג ר' שמעון בסיפא דברייתא דקתני אבל אי קדשי מזבח בעלי מומין יפדו ולימא ר' שמעון דיקברו כדאית ליה אמר לך ר"ל תני בסיפא בקדשי מזבח [בין תמימי' ובין בע"מ יקברו] הואיל וחזו למזבח ע"י פדייה. עבדו בהו מעלה חומרא דיקברו דהא אינן יוצאין מידי מזבח:
notes.en: But where their consecration preceded their blemish, what [is the law]? It requires standing and valuation. Let us say it is, etc., as we said above. If so, Rabbi Shimon should disagree in the latter clause of the baraita, which teaches: but with regard to animals consecrated for the altar, blemished ones are redeemed; and Rabbi Shimon should say that they are buried, as he holds. Reish Lakish could say to you: teach in the latter clause, regarding animals consecrated for the altar, [whether unblemished or blemished, they are buried]. Since they are fit for the altar by means of redemption, they made a stringency for them, that they be buried, since they do not leave the custody of the altar.

messages.caption: The two baraitot on consecrated animals that died, and how Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish read each one.

messages.text: @Rabbi Zeira According to Reish Lakish, who says that according to the Rabbis, animals consecrated for the altar were not included in the halakha of standing and valuation, and it is taught with regard to animals consecrated for the altar
messages.lead: § The Gemara further discusses the dispute between Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish.

notes.he: הא דקתני בהך ברייתא קדשי מזבח יפדו מוקים לה אפילו בקדם הקדישן את מומן ש"מ כו' בשלמא לר' יוחנן דמוקים לה בבעל מום מעיקרו לא איכפת לן אם נפדה לכלבים דהא לא נחתא מעולם קדושה לגופיה אלא לריש לקיש איכא למיבעי:
notes.en: According to Reish Lakish, who says that according to the Rabbis, etc.: that which is taught in this baraita, that animals consecrated for the altar are redeemed, he establishes even where their consecration preceded their blemish; conclude from it, etc. Granted, according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, who establishes it as referring to an animal blemished from the outset, it does not matter to us if it is redeemed for dogs, since sanctity never took effect on its body. But according to Reish Lakish there is a question.

messages.text: that blemished animals can be redeemed; and we established that according to Reish Lakish, the baraita is dealing with animals whose consecrations preceded their blemishes, which means that although the animal has inherent sanctity because it was consecrated when unblemished, nevertheless it can be redeemed; let us conclude from the baraita that one may redeem sacrificial animals in order to feed them to dogs.

notes.he: שמעת מינה פודין את הקדשים להאכילן לכלבים דהא כיון דמתו ופריק להו לא חזו אלא לכלבים:
notes.en: Conclude from it that one may redeem sacrificial animals to feed them to dogs: since once they have died and he redeems them, they are fit only for dogs.

messages.text: One cannot arrive at this conclusion from the baraita, since when the baraita states that the animals died it is not referring to deaths due to natural causes. Rather, what are we dealing with here? With a case where one transgressed the prohibition against slaughtering the blemished animals and slaughtered them before they were redeemed, an act that nevertheless renders them permitted for human consumption after redemption.

notes.he: הא דקתני אם מתו לא מתו ממש אלא שעבר ושחטן קודם פדיון דקאמר יפדו ויאכלו:
notes.en: What are we dealing with here: that which is taught, “if they died,” does not mean they actually died, but that one transgressed and slaughtered them before redemption; about these it says they are redeemed and eaten.

notes.he: כגון שעבר ושחטן קודם פדייה דהשתא כי פריק להו חזו למיכלנהו:
notes.en: Rather, what are we dealing with here? Where one transgressed and slaughtered them before redemption, so that now, when he redeems them, they are fit to be eaten.

messages.text: With regard to all sacrificial animals that developed a blemish and one slaughtered them,

notes.dh: כדתניא כל הקדשים שנולדו בהן מום ושחטן ר"מ אומר יקברו
notes.he: איירי בקדשי מזבח דסבר היו בכלל העמדה כר"ש ולרבי יוחנן אפי' כרבנן וחכ"א יפדו דס"ל לא היו בכלל העמדה לרשב"ל ניחא שפיר דהוא רבנן דמתני' דאמר דקדשי ב"ה היו קדשי מזבח לא היו אלא לרבי יוחנן דאמר בין לרבנן בין לר"ש קדשי מזבח היו מאן נינהו רבנן דהכא וליכא למימר שקדם מומן להקדשן ופליגי בפלוגתא דתנא דבי לוי דלעיל דבסוף פרק הנהנה מן ההקדש (מעילה יט:) גריס בהדיא קדשי מזבח תמימים ונעשו בעלי מומין ועבר ושחטן ר"מ אומר יקברו וחכ"א יפדו ובספרים כתוב ר"מ כר"ש רבנן דהכא כרבנן דהתם נימא תיהוי תיובתא דר' יוחנן אמר לך ר' יוחנן רבנן דהכא לחוד רבנן דהתם לחוד מיהו מהך דהכא איכא לדחויי דמיירי בקדשי ב"ה וחכמים היינו ר"ש אבל בפרק הנהנה במעילה (גז"ש) תניא קדשי מזבח תמימים רבי אומר יקברו וחכ"א יפדו ומההיא ודאי איכא לשנויי דרבנן דהכא לחוד ורבנן דהתם לחוד ואין לתמוה לר' יוחנן למה לו לומר כן דג' מחלוקות [יש] לימא דרבנן דהכא כרבנן דהתם קדשי מזבח לא היו י"ל דמתני' קשיא דמדקאמר ר"ש דקדשי ב"ה אם מתו יפדו מדאיצטריך לפרושי ב"ה מכלל דת"ק מיירי בהן כדפירש כל הסוגיא בספרים:
notes.en: In brief: As it is taught: all sacrificial animals that developed a blemish and one slaughtered them, Rabbi Meir says: they shall be buried: this speaks of animals consecrated for the altar; Rabbi Meir holds they were included in standing, like Rabbi Shimon (and according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, like the Rabbis too), and the Rabbis say they are redeemed because they were not included. For Reish Lakish this works well: these are the Rabbis of the mishna. But for Rabbi Yoḥanan, who says that according to both the Rabbis and Rabbi Shimon altar animals were included, who are the Rabbis here? One cannot say the case is a blemish that preceded consecration and they disagree as the tanna of the school of Levi does, for at the end of chapter HaNehene Min HaHekdesh (Me’ila 19b) the reading is explicit: altar animals that were unblemished and became blemished, and one slaughtered them: Rabbi Meir says buried, the Rabbis say redeemed. The books add: Rabbi Meir is like Rabbi Shimon, the Rabbis here are like the Rabbis there; let it be a refutation of Rabbi Yoḥanan; Rabbi Yoḥanan answers that the Rabbis here are one group and the Rabbis there another. The baraita here could instead be deflected as speaking of Temple maintenance, with “the Rabbis” being Rabbi Shimon; but in Me’ila it is taught of unblemished altar animals: Rabbi says buried, the Rabbis say redeemed, and there the only answer is that the two groups of Rabbis differ. Why would Rabbi Yoḥanan accept three disputes rather than say the Rabbis here are like the Rabbis there, that altar animals were not included? Because the mishna is difficult: since Rabbi Shimon had to specify that animals consecrated for Temple maintenance that died are redeemed, the first tanna must have spoken of them, as the books explain the whole passage. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: They shall be buried, as he holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon that animals consecrated for the altar were included in the halakha of standing and valuation and must be buried if they died.

notes.he: כר"ש דאמר קדשי מזבח היו בהעמדה והערכה:
notes.en: Rabbi Meir says: they shall be buried: like Rabbi Shimon, who says that animals consecrated for the altar were [included] in standing and valuation.

messages.text: Since an animal consecrated for the altar is not included in the halakha of standing and valuation, even if one slaughtered it, it can be redeemed.

notes.he: שלא היו בהעמדה והערכה:
notes.en: They can be redeemed: since they were not [included] in standing and valuation.

notes.he: מדר' מאיר כר' שמעון דאמר קדשי מזבח היו ויקברו:
notes.en: As it is taught, etc. And the Rabbis say: they can be redeemed. Since Rabbi Meir [holds] like Rabbi Shimon, who says that animals consecrated for the altar were [included], they are buried.

notes.he: רבנן דהכא דאמרי יפדו כרבנן דהתם דלעיל אליבא דר' שמעון בן לקיש דאמר קדשי מזבח לא היו ויפדו:
notes.en: The Rabbis here, who say they are redeemed, are like the Rabbis there above, according to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, who said that animals consecrated for the altar were not [included], and so they are redeemed.

messages.text: @Rabbi Zeira According to Rabbi Shimon, who said that animals consecrated for Temple maintenance were not included in the halakha of standing and valuation and are redeemed if they died, why does he state, in the last baraita cited earlier, that unblemished animals consecrated for Temple maintenance shall be buried and not redeemed?
It is because they are fit for sacrifice upon the altar.

notes.he: עבוד להו מעלה בתמימים דמזבח:
notes.en: Because they are fit for sacrifice: they made a stringency for them, for unblemished animals [that are fit] for the altar.

notes.he: וקשיא דא"כ מאי קאמר בפ"ק דשבועות (דף יא:) גבי פרה שנשחטה תפדה [ופריך] הא בעי' העמדה כו' ומוקי לה כר"ש דאמר קדשי ב"ה לא היו ומה בכך הא תמימים היא ותקבר מיבעי ליה וי"ל דיש חילוק בדבר דודאי כשהקדיש קדשי ב"ה תמימים עבר בבל תקדישו ושינה בהן להקדיש שלא כמצותו דמצות תמימים למזבח דין הוא לקוברן כשמתו אבל פרה שלא שינה במצותה תפדה (למה נקט אותה עוד י"ל דודאי תמימים לבדק הבית שעומדין למזבח יש לנו להחמיר דאמרת מזבח):
notes.en: Because they are fit for sacrifice: And it is difficult: if so, what does it say in the first chapter of Shevuot (11b) about a red heifer that was slaughtered, that it is redeemed? [The Gemara there] asks: but standing [and valuation] is required, etc.; and it establishes it in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, who says that animals consecrated for Temple maintenance were not [included]. But what of it? It is unblemished, and it should have said that it is buried! One can say that there is a distinction in the matter. Certainly, when one consecrated unblemished animals for Temple maintenance, he transgressed the prohibition against consecrating them [for Temple maintenance] and deviated with them, consecrating them not in accordance with their mitzva, since the mitzva for unblemished animals is the altar; it is proper to bury them when they died. But a red heifer, with which he did not deviate from its mitzva, is redeemed. (Why did he take it? Alternatively, one can say: certainly with unblemished animals for Temple maintenance, which stand to go to the altar, we must be stringent, as you said, “[fit for] the altar.”)

messages.text: The Gemara explains the significance of the fact that these animals, which were consecrated for Temple maintenance, are fit for the altar. As it is taught in a baraita:

One who associates unblemished animals, i.e., consecrates them by means of associating their sanctity with sanctified items, for Temple maintenance, when they are redeemed by the treasurer they are redeemed only for the altar, i.e., they are sold to those who must bring an offering, and the animals are sacrificed upon the altar. They may be redeemed only for the altar, not for any non-sacred use, as any consecrated item that is fit to be sacrificed on the altar may never leave the custody of the altar.

According to Rabbi Yoḥanan, who interprets the above baraita as referring to an animal blemished from the outset, and who further claims that everyone, i.e., Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis, holds that an animal blemished from the outset was not included in the halakha of standing and valuation, one may ask: And do they both agree that an animal blemished from the outset was not included in that halakha?
messages.lead: § The Gemara continues to analyze the opinions of Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish. Rav Pappa said to Abaye, and some say that Rava said to Abaye:

notes.dh: לרבי יוחנן דמוקים לה בבעל מום מעיקרו
notes.he: ואמר משום הכי לא פליג ר"ש עלה אלמא דכ"ע בעל מום מעיקרו לא בעי העמדה והערכה והתנן כו' דבשלמא לר"ל ליכא לאקשויי דהוא מוקים לה בתם ונעשה בעל מום לאחר הקדש ואיכא למימר דבעל מום מעיקרו הוי כהקדש ב"ה דאע"ג דלמזבח אקדשיה אפ"ה כבדק הבית דמי דלא קדיש אלא לדמי והוי בהעמדה והערכה לרבנן אלא לר' יוחנן קשיא:
notes.en: According to Rabbi Yoḥanan, who establishes it as referring to an animal blemished from the outset: and says that is why Rabbi Shimon does not disagree with it; evidently, according to everyone, an animal blemished from the outset does not require standing and valuation. But we learned, etc. Granted, according to Reish Lakish there is no difficulty, since he establishes it as an unblemished animal that became blemished after consecration, and one can say that an animal blemished from the outset is like a consecration for Temple maintenance: although he consecrated it for the altar, it is nevertheless like Temple maintenance, since it is consecrated only for its value, and it is [included] in standing and valuation according to the Rabbis. But according to Rabbi Yoḥanan it is difficult.

messages.text: But didn’t we learn in a mishna (Bekhorot 14a):

All the sacrificial animals in which a permanent blemish preceded their consecration are not sanctified as offerings; rather, they are sold and the money received is used to purchase valid offerings. And once they are redeemed, they are obligated in, i.e., subject to accounting their offspring, a firstborn; and in the priestly gifts of the foreleg, jaw, and maw; and they emerge from their sacred status and assume complete non-sacred status in order to be shorn and to be utilized for labor.

notes.he: זרוע ולחיים וקיבה:
notes.en: And in the gifts: the foreleg, the jaw and the maw.

notes.he: לאחר פדיונן:
notes.en: To be shorn and to be utilized for labor: after their redemption.

messages.text: And their offspring and their milk are permitted after their redemption. And one who slaughters them outside the Temple courtyard is exempt from karet, even if the animal was not yet redeemed, and those animals do not render an animal exchanged for them a substitute. And if these animals died before they were redeemed, they may be redeemed.

notes.he: אפילו איעבר קודם פדיונן ואיתיליד לאחר פדיונן:
notes.en: Their offspring and their milk are permitted: even if [the offspring] was conceived before their redemption and born after their redemption.

messages.text: With regard to this mishna: This statement, that one who consecrates a blemished animal for the altar may redeem it if it dies, is in accordance with the statement of Rabbi Shimon, who says that animals consecrated for the altar were included in the halakha of standing and valuation, but animals consecrated for Temple maintenance were not included.
messages.quote: And if these animals died before they were redeemed, they may be redeemed

notes.he: עלה בפרק שני דבכורות הא דתנן יפדו זו דברי ר"ש דאמר קדשי ב"ה אם מתו יפדו והאי בעל מום מעיקרו כקדשי בדק הבית חשיב ליה אבל חכמים כו':
notes.en: And Rav said: about it, in the second chapter of Bekhorot: that which we learned, “they may be redeemed,” is the statement of Rabbi Shimon, who says that animals consecrated for Temple maintenance, if they died, are redeemed; and he considers this animal blemished from the outset like animals consecrated for Temple maintenance. But the Rabbis, etc.

notes.he: זו דברי ר' שמעון דאמר קדשי בדק הבית אם מתו יפדו דלא היו בכלל העמדה והערכה והני קדש' שקדם מומן [בקדש] את הקדישן אע"ג דקדשי מזבח נינהו כיון דלא חל עליהן הקדש גמור למזבח הלכך דיניהו כקדשי בדק הבית דאם מתו יפדו דלא היו בכלל העמדה והערכה:
notes.en: [An editorial note says this is Rabbeinu Gershom’s reading as given in the Shitah Mekubetzet.] Let us say it is a conclusive refutation, etc. This is the statement of Rabbi Shimon, who says that animals consecrated for Temple maintenance, if they died, are redeemed, since they were not included in standing and valuation. And these consecrated animals whose blemish preceded their consecration, even though they are consecrated for the altar, since a full consecration for the altar did not take effect on them, their law is therefore like that of animals consecrated for Temple maintenance: if they died they are redeemed, since they were not included in standing and valuation.

messages.text: If animals consecrated for Temple maintenance died, they can be redeemed, since they were not included in the halakha of standing and valuation. But animals consecrated for the altar that died are buried, as they were included in this halakha.

And Rabbi Shimon concedes with regard to an animal that was blemished from the outset, which was consecrated for the altar and died, that it is redeemed. What is the reason? As the verse states: “Then he shall set the animal before the priest. And the priest shall value it” (Leviticus 27:11–12). The emphasis of “it” serves to exclude an animal that was blemished from the outset from the halakha of standing and valuation.

verse.he: וְאִם כׇּל־בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה אֲשֶׁר לֹא־יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה קׇרְבָּן לַיהֹוָה וְהֶעֱמִיד אֶת־הַבְּהֵמָה לִפְנֵי הַכֹּהֵן׃ וְהֶעֱרִיךְ הַכֹּהֵן אֹתָהּ בֵּין טוֹב וּבֵין רָע כְּעֶרְכְּךָ הַכֹּהֵן כֵּן יִהְיֶה׃
verse.en: If [the vow concerns] any impure animal that may not be brought as an offering to GOD, the animal shall be presented before the priest, and the priest shall assess it. Whether high or low, whatever assessment is set by the priest shall stand;

messages.text: But the Rabbis say: Every animal consecrated for the altar, even one that was blemished from the outset, was included in the halakha of standing and valuation, and must be buried if it dies.
This apparently contradicts the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan, who says that according to the Rabbis an animal that was blemished from the outset was not included in the halakha of standing and valuation.

notes.he: הכל היו בכלל [העמדה והערכה] אפי' קדשי בדק הבית אפי' בעל מום מעיקרו. וקשיא לר' יוחנן דאמר אותה לרבנן למעוטי בעל מום מעיקרא דלא היו דקס"ד דהא חכמים היינו רבנן דפליגי אדר' שמעון:
notes.en: But the Sages say: all were included [in standing and valuation], even animals consecrated for Temple maintenance, even one blemished from the outset. And this is difficult for Rabbi Yoḥanan, who says that “it,” according to the Rabbis, serves to exclude one blemished from the outset, which was not [included]; for it now enters our mind that these Sages are the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Shimon.

messages.text: The statement of Rav Yehuda in the name of Rav does not pose a difficulty for Rabbi Yoḥanan, as Rav was not referring to the Rabbis of the mishna, who disagree with Rabbi Shimon. Rather, who is the tanna referred to here as the Rabbis? It is a tanna of the school of Levi.
messages.lead: Abaye said to Rav Pappa, or Rava:

notes.he: מאן חכמים תנא דבי לוי אבל רבנן דבפלוגתא דר' שמעון בבעלי מומין מעיקרא כר' שמעון סבירא להו:
notes.en: He said to him: No. Who are the Sages? The tanna of the school of Levi. But the Rabbis in the dispute with Rabbi Shimon hold, with regard to animals blemished from the outset, like Rabbi Shimon.

messages.text: If so, that even the Rabbis of the mishna hold that an animal that was blemished from the outset is redeemed, why did Rav Yehuda say that Rav said that this mishna in tractate Bekhorot is in accordance with the statement of Rabbi Shimon, and nothing more? This statement indicates that the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon alone. He should have said that this mishna is in accordance with the statement of Rabbi Shimon and those who disagree with him, i.e., the Rabbis.
messages.lead: The other rabbi questioned Abaye’s answer:
messages.quote: This statement … is in accordance with the statement of Rabbi Shimon

notes.he: דהא רבנן דפליגי עליה נמי אוקמת דבעל מום מעיקרו לא הוה בכלל העמדה והערכה: להכי לא אמר רב זו דברי ר"ש ומחלוקתו דאיהו סבר לה כר' שמעון בן לקיש דאמר לרבנן קדשי מזבח לא היו בכלל העמדה והערכה והלכך לא מיתוקמא ההיא דבכורות כולה כרבנן משום דרישא דההיא דמיירי בבעל מום מעיקרו דתני יפדו מתוקמא אפילו לרבנן אבל סיפא קתני אבל קדשים שקדם הקדישן את מומן אם מתו יקברו לא אתיא כרבנן הלכך לא מיתוקמא כרבנן דהכא:
notes.en: And his disputants: since you have established that the Rabbis who disagree with him also [hold] that an animal blemished from the outset was not included in standing and valuation. [And] the reason Rav did not say “this is the statement of Rabbi Shimon and his disputants” is that he holds like Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, who said that according to the Rabbis animals consecrated for the altar were not included in standing and valuation. Therefore that [mishna] in Bekhorot cannot be established entirely according to the Rabbis: its first clause, which speaks of an animal blemished from the outset and teaches “they may be redeemed,” can be established even according to the Rabbis; but the latter clause teaches, “But sacrificial animals whose consecration preceded their blemish, if they died, they shall be buried,” which does not accord with the Rabbis. Therefore it cannot be established according to the Rabbis here.

messages.text: The reason that Rav Yehuda does not teach in this manner, i.e., he does not say that the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, is because Rav holds in accordance with the opinion of Reish Lakish, who said that according to the Rabbis of the mishna, only animals consecrated for Temple maintenance were included in the halakha of standing and valuation; animals consecrated for the altar were not included, and are therefore redeemed.

notes.dh: אי הכי זו דברי ר' שמעון
notes.he: [ומחלוקתו מיבעי למימר לרב א"ל רבא רב כריש לקיש סבירא ליה דאמר דלרבנן קדשי מזבח לא היו ולא מתוקמא סיפא כרבנן דקתני בשקדם הקדישן את מומן ואם מתו יקברו ואי רבנן כיון דאמרי דקדשי מזבח לא היו אמאי יקברו הלכך לא מיתמ' ליה זו דברי ר' שמעון ומחלוקתו. אבל כר' שמעון (ומחלוקתו) מיתוקמא סיפא נמי דהא בין ר' יוחנן בין ר"ל מודו דלר' שמעון קדשי מזבח היו הלכך כי קדם הקדישן את מומן יקברו אבל בבעל מום מעיקרא היינו שקדם מומן להקדישן מודה ר"ש דלא היו בכלל יפדה:
notes.en: If so, “this is the statement of Rabbi Shimon” — Rav should have said “and his disputants.” Rava said to him [Rabbeinu Gershom’s text names Rava as the one who answers]: Rav holds like Reish Lakish, who says that according to the Rabbis animals consecrated for the altar were not [included], and the latter clause cannot be established according to the Rabbis, since it teaches: where their consecration preceded their blemish, if they died, they shall be buried. If it were the Rabbis, since they say that animals consecrated for the altar were not [included], why would they be buried? Therefore he cannot say “this is the statement of Rabbi Shimon and his disputants.” But according to Rabbi Shimon the latter clause too can be established, since both Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish agree that according to Rabbi Shimon animals consecrated for the altar were [included]; therefore, when their consecration preceded their blemish, they are buried. But with an animal blemished from the outset, that is, where its blemish preceded its consecration, Rabbi Shimon concedes that it was not included, and it is redeemed.

messages.text: And admittedly the first clause of the mishna can be explained in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, as it teaches that if they died they can be redeemed. This ruling is in accordance with the Rabbis, as an animal that was blemished from the outset is considered as one consecrated for the altar, since as it was consecrated in order to be sold to purchase a valid offering.

But the latter clause of the mishna, which discusses a case where the consecration of the animal preceded the development of a blemish, is not in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, as it teaches that if they died they shall be buried. According to Reish Lakish and Rav, the Rabbis hold that in such a case the animal is redeemed. Consequently, the mishna cannot be in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis.

And if you wish, say instead that Rav holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan, that the Rabbis maintain that all consecrations were included in the halakha of standing and valuation and are buried if they died, and the mishna is in fact in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis.

notes.dh: ואיבעית אימא רב כר' יוחנן ס"ל
notes.he: דאחד קדשי מזבח ואחד קדשי ב"ה בעי העמדה והערכה חוץ מבעל מום מעיקרו ובין רישא וסיפא דההיא מצי לאוקומה נמי כרבנן וכר"ש ותני זו דברי רבי שמעון ומחלוקתו:
notes.en: And if you wish, say that Rav holds like Rabbi Yoḥanan: that both animals consecrated for the altar and those consecrated for Temple maintenance require standing and valuation, except for an animal blemished from the outset; and both the first and the latter clauses of that [mishna] can be established also according to the Rabbis, as well as according to Rabbi Shimon, and he teaches: “This is the statement of Rabbi Shimon and his disputants.”

notes.he: ואב"א אפי' תימא סבר לה רב כרבי יוחנן דאמר דלרבנן אחד זה ואחד זה היו ומודין בבעל מום מעיקרא דלא היו:
notes.en: And if you wish, say: you may even say that Rav holds like Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said that according to the Rabbis both this and that were [included], and they agree with regard to an animal blemished from the outset that it was not.

messages.text: And as for that which posed a difficulty for you, that Rav Yehuda should have said that this mishna is in accordance with the statement of Rabbi Shimon and those who disagree with him, say: Indeed he said so, that the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon and those who disagree with him.

notes.he: ודקא קשיא לך א"כ רישא וסיפא מיתוקמא נמי כרבנן א"כ לימא זו דברי ר' שמעון ומחלוקתו תני הכי ולא תיקשה]:
notes.en: And as for what was difficult for you: if so, the first and latter clauses can be established also according to the Rabbis, so let him say “this is the statement of Rabbi Shimon and his disputants”; teach it so, and there is no difficulty.

messages.text: Mishna

And these are the items that are buried from which deriving benefit is forbidden: In the case of a sacrificial animal that miscarried, the fetus shall be buried. If the animal miscarried a placenta, the placenta shall be buried.

notes.he: הנפלים:
notes.en: Mishna: they shall be buried: the miscarried fetuses.

notes.he: שאין שליא בלא ולד. וכל הנך נקברים משום דאיסורי הנאה נינהו:
notes.en: A placenta shall be buried: since there is no placenta without a fetus. And all of these are buried because they are forbidden for benefit.

notes.he: דכל הני אסור' בהנאה:
notes.en: Mishna: These are the items that are buried: for all of these are forbidden for benefit.

messages.text: And the same halakha applies to an ox that is stoned for killing a person; and a heifer whose neck is broken when a corpse is found between two cities and the killer is unknown; and the birds brought by a leper for purification; and the hair of a nazirite who became ritually impure, who shaves his head before beginning a new term of naziriteship.

And the same halakha applies to the firstborn of a donkey that, if it is not redeemed with a sheep, has its neck broken; and a forbidden mixture of meat cooked in milk; and non-sacred animals that were slaughtered in the Temple courtyard.

notes.he: ל"ק הא דקתני ומפטר חמור בשק ידלק היינו כשארג השער בשק דאי אמרת נקבר זמנין דמשכחת ליה איניש (והיה) [ויהיה] משתמש בו הלכך ידלק. הא בשער אבל בשער של פטר חמור שאינו ארוג יקבר שאפילו אם יבוא לידי אדם לאחר מיכן יניחנו דאינו ראוי לכלום. ובפלוגתא האי ובפלוגתא היינו כמו כתנאי אלא משום דר' יוסי ב"ר חנינא אמורא הוי מש"ה נקיט האי לישנא בפלוגתא:
notes.en: [This note concerns the Gemara on 34a, which contrasts this mishna with a mishna in Orla.] There is no difficulty: that which is taught, “and from a firstborn donkey, in a sack, it shall be burned,” is where he wove the hair into a sack; for if you say it is buried, sometimes a person may find it and use it; therefore it is burned. That is with [woven] hair; but the hair of a firstborn donkey that is not woven is buried, for even if it comes into a person’s hands afterward, he will leave it, as it is not fit for anything. And “in a dispute”: this “in a dispute” is like “as tanna’im,” except that because Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, was an Amora, he used this expression “in a dispute.”

messages.text: Non-sacred animals that were slaughtered in the Temple courtyard shall be burned, like sacrificial animals that were disqualified in the courtyard. And likewise, an undomesticated animal that was slaughtered in the Temple courtyard, although it is not similar to the animals sacrificed in the Temple, shall be burned by rabbinic decree.

notes.he: משום דמיחלפי בהו קדשים שאירע בהו פסול דאי אמר יקברו כיון דלא מוכחא מילתא אי חולין הוו אי קדשים אתו למימר נמי קדשים שאירע בהן פסול טומאה או פסול נותר יקברו וקיימא לן בפסחים בפ"ב (דף כד.) בקדש באש תשרף לימד על כל הפסולין שבקדש שהן בשרפה:
notes.en: Non-sacred animals that were slaughtered in the courtyard shall be burned: because sacrificial animals that incurred a disqualification would be confused with them. For if he said they are buried, since it is not evident whether they were non-sacred or sacrificial, people would come to say that sacrificial animals that incurred a disqualification of impurity or of notar are also buried. And we hold, in the second chapter of Pesaḥim (24a), that “In the holy place… it shall be burned with fire” [Leviticus 6:23] teaches about all the disqualified [items] among consecrated items, that they are to be burned.

notes.he: אפי' אם חולין היא דליכא למיגזר משום דלא ליקבור קדשים פסולין דהא כ"ע ידעי דחיה במוקדשים ליכא ולא אתי לחלופי אפילו הכי תשרף:
notes.en: And likewise an undomesticated animal that was slaughtered in the courtyard: even if it is non-sacred, where there is no [reason] to decree lest people bury disqualified sacrificial animals, since everyone knows that there are no undomesticated animals among consecrated animals and they will not come to confuse them; even so it is burned.

notes.dh: ר' שמעון אומר חולין שנשחטו בעזרה ישרפו מ"ט ישרפו
notes.he: דדינו כקדשים שנשחטו חוץ למקומן מה הנך ישרפו דשינה דרכן אף חולין דשינה דרכן ישרפו. וקדשים שנשחטו חוץ למקומן מנלן דכתיב וכל חטאת אשר יובא את דמה וגו' לימד דכל ששינה מקומו דישרף ל"ק הא בנזיר טמא הא בנזיר טהור. הא דקתני משער נזיר בשק ידלק היינו בשער נזיר טמא [נ' טהור] משום דדינו היינו לשלח תחת הדוד ולשרף הלכך נשרף. והא דתני יקבר היינו בשער נזיר טהור [נ' טמא]:
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon says: non-sacred animals that were slaughtered in the courtyard shall be burned. What is the reason they are burned? Because their law is like that of sacrificial animals that were slaughtered outside their place: just as those are burned because their manner was changed, so too non-sacred animals whose manner was changed are burned. And from where do we derive that sacrificial animals slaughtered outside their place [are burned]? As it is written: “And any sin offering whose blood is brought,” etc. [Leviticus 6:23]; this teaches that anything whose place was changed is burned. [The rest of the note concerns the Gemara on 34a.] There is no difficulty: this is with an impure nazirite, that is with a pure nazirite. That which is taught, “from the hair of a nazirite, in a sack, it shall be burned,” is with the hair of an impure nazirite [a correction reads: pure], since his law is to send it under the pot and burn it; therefore it is burned. And that which is taught, “it shall be buried,” is with the hair of a pure nazirite [a correction reads: impure].

messages.text: And these are the items that are burned: Leavened bread on Passover shall be burned. And the same halakha applies to ritually impure teruma.

notes.he: בפסחים מפרש טעמא בפרק כל שעה (פסחים דף כז:) דגמר ליה מנותר:
notes.en: Leavened bread on Passover: the reason is explained in Pesaḥim, in chapter Kol Sha’ah (Pesaḥim 27b): he derives it from notar.

notes.he: נמי תשרף. בבמה מדליקין (שבת כה.) מפרש טעמא דמותרת בהנאה דאמרינן נמי התם בפרק כל שעה (פסחים דף כג.) לך ניתנה להסיקה תחת תבשילך:
notes.en: Impure teruma: is also burned. In Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 25a) the reason is explained that it is permitted for benefit, as we also say there in chapter Kol Sha’ah (Pesaḥim 23a): “To you it was given, to burn under your cooked food.”

messages.text: And with regard to the fruit that grows on a tree during the three years after it was planted [orla], and diverse kinds of food crops sown in a vineyard, those items whose appropriate manner of destruction is to be burned, e.g., foods, shall be burned; and those items whose appropriate manner of destruction is to be buried, e.g., liquids, shall be buried.

notes.he: פן תקדש המלאה וגו' פן תוקד אש וערלה מכלאים גמרה:
notes.en: Diverse kinds in a vineyard: “lest the fullness be forfeited [tikdash],” etc. [read as] “lest a fire be kindled [tukad]”; and orla is derived from diverse kinds.

notes.he: אערלה וכלאי הכרם קאי. אוכלין ישרפו ומשקין יקברו:
notes.en: Those whose manner, etc.: refers to orla and diverse kinds in a vineyard: foods are burned and liquids are buried.

notes.dh: אלו הן הנשרפין ערלה וכלאי הכרם
notes.he: צריך עיון בשלמא בכלאי הכרם דהא כתיבי פן תקדש המלאה פן תוקד אש אלא ערלה צריך עיון טעמא מאי בשרפה ופי' רש"י משום דאיתקש לכלאי הכרם:
notes.en: These are the items that are burned: orla and diverse kinds in a vineyard: this requires examination. Granted with regard to diverse kinds in a vineyard, since it is written “lest the fullness be forfeited [tikdash],” [read as] “lest it be kindled [tukad] with fire.” But with regard to orla this requires examination: what is the reason it is burned? And Rashi explained: because it is juxtaposed with diverse kinds in a vineyard.

messages.text: And one may ignite a fire with bread and with oil of impure teruma, even though the priest derives benefit from that fire.

notes.he: ליהנות בפת ובשמן של תרומה:
notes.en: And one may ignite: to derive benefit from bread and from oil of teruma.

messages.text: And with regard to all sacrificial animals that were slaughtered with the intent to sacrifice or consume them beyond their designated time or outside their designated place, those animals shall be burned.

notes.he: כלומר ע"מ לאכלן חוץ לזמנן או לאכלן חוץ למקומן:
notes.en: Beyond their time: that is, with the intent to eat them beyond their time or to eat them outside their place.

notes.he: כדפירשתי לעיל לימד על כל פסולין שבקדש כו':
notes.en: Shall be burned: as I explained above: it teaches about all the disqualified [items] among consecrated items, etc.

notes.dh: הנשרפין אפרן מותר ונקברים אפרן אסור
notes.he: צריך עיון טעמא מאי ואומר מורי הרמ"ר דנשרפין כיון שצוה הכתוב לשורפן אחר שעשה כאילו נעשית מצותו ואין לך דבר שנעשית מצותו ומועלין בו ה"נ כיון שנעשית מצותו הלך אסוריה והא דאמר אשירה אסורה לעולם אף על פי שהזקיק הכתוב לשורפה (דברים יב) היינו משום דכתיב (שם יג) לא ידבק בידך מאומה מן החרם אבל הנקברין דלא הטעין הכתוב לשורפן משוך איסורייהו לעולם:
notes.en: Items that are burned, their ashes are permitted; items that are buried, their ashes are forbidden [a principle stated in the Gemara on 34a]: this requires examination: what is the reason? And my teacher, the Ramar, says: as for items that are burned, since the verse commanded to burn them, once one has done so it is as though its mitzva has been performed, and there is nothing whose mitzva has been performed that is subject to misuse; here too, since its mitzva has been performed, its prohibition is gone. And that which is said, that an ashera is forbidden forever even though the verse requires it to be burned (Deuteronomy 12), is because it is written: “And there shall cleave nothing of the devoted thing to your hand” (Deuteronomy 13). But items that are buried, which the verse did not require to be burned, their prohibition continues forever.

messages.text: Continues on 34a: the mishna’s list of items that are burned goes on with the provisional guilt offering and the bird sin offering brought for an uncertainty, and then states the principle that items that are buried are not burned, and items that are burned are not buried.
